reasoning: Short i then long aa, taa marbuta as e after ي: wilaaye. Used of an American state and in il-wilaayaat il-mutta7ide.
Emphatic ص as S and ق as a glottal stop: Sa'r. It covers falcons as well as hawks, and is also a man's name, where the q is often kept.
In a construct مرة becomes mart, as in mart 3ammi, so I respell it مَرْت. khaal is the mother's brother, so his wife is mart khaal; usually said with a pronoun, mart khaali.
ع is 3, short u then a final cluster: 3urs, plural a3raas. The wedding celebration itself, not the legal marriage.
Fatha, sukun, taa marbuta as e after و: rakwe. The long-handled pot Arabic coffee is boiled in.
ح is 7 and ق is a glottal stop: mas7uu'. MSA in origin and mostly seen on packaging; in Ramallah kitchens people more often name the brand or say buudra.
CiCiC past in Palestinian with ح as 7 and ق as a glottal stop: li7i', imperfect yil7a'. Used both for catching up with someone and for making it in time.
il- assimilates to the sun letter ن, with the shadda doubling it: in-nuur. The set reply to masa il-kheer.
A short fatha closed by a glottal stop, written ': la'. The ordinary spoken 'no', against written laa.
Long oo, not uu: toom. The Palestinian form of ثوم, already respelled with ت in the entry, which matches what is said.
ذ is realised as plain z in this verb in Ramallah, so I respell ذكرني as زَكِّرْنِي; the shadda doubles the ك. Form II imperative to a man with the object -ni.
Form II with the shadda doubling س: fassar, imperfect bifassir. Also used of interpreting a dream.
Fatha then a short front vowel, written i since the scheme has no short e, with ح as 7: rashi7. Said as 3indi rashi7, 'I have a cold'.
bi- plus the article assimilates to the sun letter ت: bit-tawfii', with ق as a glottal stop. The hamza is written after the prefix in bil-'imti7aan.
ص is a sun letter, so the article assimilates and the shadda doubles the emphatic whole: iS-Soomaal, with long oo then aa.
Initial hamza written as the vowel, long ii: injiil. Strictly the Gospel or New Testament; the whole Bible is il-kitaab il-muqaddas, though il-injiil is used loosely for it.
ق glottalises even in this religious formula and the shadda doubles ب: ta'abbal allah. Said in Ramadan and after prayer, often extended with Taa3atkum.
In the construct the taa marbuta is pronounced t, so I respell فاتورة as فَاتُورَت. mayy is the Palestinian 'water', with a doubled final y.
shu is the Palestinian 'what'; akhbaar begins with a bare vowel but the hamza of il-'awlaad is written after the article prefix. The question mark is not romanized.
fii is the existential 'there is', so as a question it means 'is there'. 3addaad has the shadda doubling د: a taxi meter, or a utility meter.
'addeesh has a glottal ق, a doubled د and ee. The participle saakin carries the present sense, and hoon 'here' has oo.
Initial hamza is written as the bare vowel and the dual ending is -een: alfeen.
Taa marbuta as e after ب: maktabe. One word for both a bookshop and a library, as the entry says.
b-imperfect third masculine singular of سوي: biswa, 'it is worth it'. Negated as ma biswa.
Palestinian prefix yi- on both verbs, ح as 7 and غ as gh, with the masculine suffix -o. Said of someone who has died.
